selected.name: Principled simplification
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the work removes complexity or parameters, demonstrates that the retained mechanism suffices, and explains why omitted components are unnecessary; score 0 when it merely adds modules without necessity evidence.
selected.rationale: R18 shows that many diffusion components are nonessential for representation learning, while R20 argues that a large learned classifier can be fixed with little loss.
member_names: Clear Translation of Theory to Practice
Contribution by subtraction rather than addition

selected.name: Task-matched structural bias
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the architecture or representation encodes the task’s relevant geometry, hierarchy, symmetry, or compositional structure and the connection is explained; score 0 when the architecture is generic with no task-specific structural rationale.
selected.rationale: R10 introduces higher-order attention for logical reasoning, while R30 uses hyperbolic geometry for hierarchical linguistic structure.

selected.name: States a limit, bound, or guarantee on what is achievable
selected.instruction: Score whether the abstract makes a claim about the boundary of the possible, with its regime stated. 10 = an explicit upper or lower bound, near-optimality, provable separation or margin, existence claim, or complexity result, together with the conditions under which it holds. 5 = a theoretical framework or convergence claim asserted without the regime being visible. 0 = the abstract makes only empirical claims about how one system performed.
selected.rationale: R09 sandwiches the rate-distortion function and converts the bound into a statement about how much room existing compressors have left; R15 gives an O(m + poly(k/eps)) coreset and argues the dependence on m is nearly optimal; R53 characterises benign, tempered and catastrophic overfitting; R05 guarantees a distinguishable margin; R43 frames model utilisation as an optimisation problem with near-optimal solutions. All are dense-high with card scores between 0.006 and 0.34. A scorecard with a generic 'theoretical grounding' criterion cannot tell a bound on the achievable from a convergence proof attached to a specific algorithm (R40).
member_names: States a limit, bound, or guarantee on what is achievable

selected.name: Efficiency-quality integration
selected.instruction: Score 10 when resource savings are quantified together with preservation or improvement of the task capability, including relevant end-to-end costs; score 0 when efficiency is asserted without accounting or quality evidence.
selected.rationale: R06 ties batch scaling to training time without accuracy degradation, R22 quantifies training-time reduction and accuracy, and R24 connects extreme quantization to single-GPU inference and measured speedups.

selected.name: Extensible method interface
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the contribution is presented as a reusable module, framework, or interface that naturally applies across architectures, tasks, or problem instances; score 0 when it is tightly specialized to one dataset, model, or pipeline with no evident reuse path.
selected.rationale: R35 describes embedding and matching mechanisms reusable as plugins, R47 emphasizes integration with fields and fast multipole methods, and R16 improves an existing set-prediction network through a broadly applicable optimization technique.

selected.name: Explicit Epistemic Uncertainty Modeling
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the method explicitly models, quantifies, or relies on epistemic uncertainty, task ambiguity, or model confidence in its core algorithm. Score 0 if the method treats the model as a deterministic black box without any measure of uncertainty.
selected.rationale: Dense-high abstracts incorporate epistemic uncertainty centrally (R20 CBOP uncertainty bounds, R11 DrugFlow OOD estimates, R56 label uncertainty), unlike dense-low abstracts (R03 WavTokenizer, R29 OPTQ).
member_names: Bayesian Frameworks Together With Epistemic Uncertainty Quantification

selected.name: Explains the underlying mechanism, not just the effect
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 how explicitly the abstract explains WHY the method or phenomenon works, versus merely reporting THAT it works. A 10: the abstract states an explicit causal/mechanistic account (e.g., a named mechanism, an interplay of factors, a hypothesis about cause) that is argued or shown to connect the intervention to the outcome. A 0: the abstract only states what was built/done and that it improved a number, with zero explanation of why the improvement occurs.
selected.rationale: R08 (Supervision Complexity) builds a theoretical mechanism (alignment between teacher supervision and student NTK) that explains why distillation tricks work; R41 (CBOP) explains its gain via an explicit epistemic-uncertainty tradeoff mechanism. Both are dense_high_card_low. Contrast with R01, which reports an AP gain with two named techniques but no mechanism for why distillation specifically fails on detection beyond restating the problem.
member_names: Diagnosis paired with the intervention it predicts
Explains the underlying mechanism, not just the effect

selected.name: Uncertainty-aware decision design
selected.instruction: Score 10 when uncertainty is estimated meaningfully and directly controls conservative behavior, extrapolation, or trust in model predictions; score 0 when uncertainty is absent or mentioned only as an unvalidated auxiliary output.
selected.rationale: R20 detects out-of-distribution molecules, R55 trades model-based and model-free estimates using epistemic uncertainty, and R58 uses energy margins for graph OOD detection.

selected.name: Representation fidelity
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the abstract tests whether learned representations preserve the intended semantics, structure, or causal feature under controlled perturbations or transfers; score 0 when representation quality is inferred only from an unrelated task metric.
selected.rationale: R24 tests transfer of implicit logical structure across visually dissimilar tasks, while R54 probes whether language and visual representations share the claimed semantic structure.

selected.name: Evaluation construct validity
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the dataset, metric, and protocol directly measure the phenomenon claimed, including appropriate granularity and human or expert grounding where needed; score 0 when the evaluation proxy is weakly related to the claim.
selected.rationale: R01 spans modalities, difficulty levels, anomaly localization, and explanations, R21 validates implicitness against human judgments, and R51 uses expert cuneiform annotations for fine-grained structure.

selected.name: Theory–experiment agreement
selected.instruction: Score 10 when formal analysis yields predictions or explanations that are directly tested by experiments; score 0 when theoretical claims and empirical demonstrations are largely disconnected.
selected.rationale: R04 constructs a toy dynamics whose rigorous analysis explains observed edge-of-stability behavior, and R52 links supervision-complexity theory to online-distillation experiments.

selected.name: Identifying Fundamental Flaws Together With Mathematical Resolution
selected.instruction: 10 = articulates a fundamental theoretical flaw or unrecognized paradox in widely-used methods and mathematically resolves it; 0 = identifies a minor empirical bug and provides an ad-hoc patch.
selected.rationale: The dense model rewards the discovery of fundamental theoretical flaws (R39, R48, R17, R05), while the scorecard over-credits minor engineering bug fixes (R24, R34).
member_names: Identification of Flaws in Standard Paradigms
Identifying Fundamental Flaws Together With Mathematical Resolution

selected.name: Proprietary system and dataset branding
selected.instruction: Extent to which the abstract introduces and repeatedly capitalizes a specific, branded name for the proposed method, architecture, or dataset (e.g., acronyms or portmanteaus like 'ProtoSnap', 'PERSONALITYBench'). Do not judge if the name is good or clever, only count the extent of branded proper nouns.
selected.rationale: A feature-matching model often relies on explicit cues and may give high scores to texts that use catchy, branded acronyms. An end-to-end model focuses on semantics rather than branding. Seen prominently in R01, R02, and R60.
upstream_parent_all_members: author's practice in the conference format

selected.name: Abstract length / verbosity
selected.instruction: On a scale of 0 (extremely terse, a few short sentences) to 10 (extremely long and verbose, many sentences with elaborate qualification), rate how LONG and VERBOSE the abstract text is -- word count, sentence count, and density of qualifying/elaborating clauses. Score only the extent of length/verbosity; do not judge whether the length is appropriate or whether the paper is good.
selected.rationale: Sheer length/verbosity is a stylistic and space-allocation choice, not a measure of the underlying contribution: R43 (dense_pct=.999) states its whole idea in about three terse sentences, while R33 and R08 run many sentences of elaboration; a scorer that rewards elaboration would systematically favor the latter regardless of whether the terse item is actually the stronger piece of research.
member_names: Sheer abstract length and clause verbosity

selected.name: Formatting residue
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract contains extraction, editing, or layout artifacts such as broken hyphenation, irregular spacing, bullet fragments, malformed URLs, or inconsistent TeX formatting; do not judge whether the underlying work is good.
selected.rationale: R18 contains broken lineation and hyphenation, R19 has fragmented words, and R34 includes a malformed duplicated URL, leaving visible process fingerprints unrelated to research quality.

selected.name: Unhedged superlative/promotional adjective density
selected.instruction: Rate 0-10 how densely the abstract uses unhedged superlative or promotional adverbs/adjectives (e.g., 'remarkably', 'significantly outperforms', 'notably', 'surprisingly', 'novel and comprehensive'). 0 = flat, unadorned reporting with no such language, 10 = the abstract is saturated with such promotional language. Score only the density of this promotional language, not whether the claims it dresses up are true or the work is good.
selected.rationale: Adjectives like 'Remarkably' (R23) and phrasing like 'significantly outperforming the state-of-the-art' (R33) are self-promotional dressing that some authors apply liberally and others, e.g. R12's flat 'Here we show...', avoid entirely; this rhetorical habit can move a criterion-based judge's impression without reflecting any difference in the work itself.
selected.upstream_parent: author's self-promotional practice developed through venue experience
upstream_parent_all_members: author's self-promotional practice developed through venue experience
the writer's promotional habit and the amount of polishing or writing assistance applied before submission

selected.name: Density of quantified head-to-head improvement numerals
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how densely the text carries explicit numeric performance figures attached to comparisons. Count percentages, absolute metric points, multiplicative speedups, named metric abbreviations tied to numbers (AUROC, AP, F1, FID, PSNR, dB), and before/after phrasings such as 'from 30% to 73%' or 'reduces error by 43%'. Anchors: 0 = no performance numerals anywhere; 3 = a single vague number; 6 = two or three numeric comparisons; 10 = many precise numeric deltas, several tied to named baselines or named metrics. Score only presence and density of such numerals. You must NOT judge whether the numbers are large, correct, fairly obtained or impressive, and not whether the work is good.
selected.rationale: Whether an abstract can display numeric deltas is largely decided by subfield convention, not by how much was learned: a coreset bound or a deconstruction study has nothing of this shape to report. A criterion bank that asks 'are improvements quantified against baselines?' converts that convention into score. Number-dense items here are dense_low_card_high: R03 (92.7% versus 28.5%), R35 (43.9 AP, 4.1 higher), R45 (43%), R58 (66.47% F1), R08 (40% compression, 0.5% versus 2.8% drop), R59 (3.25x, 4.5x). Number-free items are dense_high_card_low: R06, R12, R25, R27, R42, R43. Tagged mixed because a subfield's measurement culture can also drive real rigour, and R01, R07, R48 and R56 carry numerals on the other side of the slice.
member_names: Density of quantified head-to-head improvement numerals
selected.upstream_parent: reporting conventions of the author's subfield (empirical benchmark culture versus theoretical or conceptual culture)
upstream_parent_all_members: reporting conventions of the author's subfield (empirical benchmark culture versus theoretical or conceptual culture)

selected.name: Artifact-availability boilerplate and repository links
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent of explicit availability statements for code, data, models or a project page. Look for URLs (github.com, project pages), and for phrases such as 'the code is available at', 'publicly available', 'codes have been released', 'our data and code can be found at', 'model weights and data are public'. Anchors: 0 = no mention of any artifact being available; 3 = a bare unlinked mention such as 'code will be released'; 6 = one explicit link or one clear availability sentence; 10 = a prominent availability sentence naming several artifact types (code, data, checkpoints, benchmark) with URLs. Do not visit or evaluate any link, and do not judge whether releasing artifacts is good practice or whether the work is good. Presence and prominence of the boilerplate only.
selected.rationale: Release practice is set by lab norms and engineering headcount, not by the merit of the idea, but it leaves a crisp textual trace that a criterion bank almost certainly has a criterion for ('are artifacts available?'). In this slice, availability boilerplate clusters hard on the dense_low_card_high side: R32, R36, R51, R59, R16, R05, R34, R29, R39. Items with no availability sentence at all cluster on the dense_high_card_low side: R06, R11, R27, R42, R22, R44. Tagged mixed because well-resourced labs that release code may also produce better work; R37 shows the trace is not deterministic.
selected.upstream_parent: the producing lab's engineering resources and open-source release practice
upstream_parent_all_members: author's/lab's institutional practice and resourcing for packaging code releases
the producing lab's engineering resources and open-source release practice

selected.name: Numerical spectacle
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract foregrounds exact percentages, speedups, benchmark gains, or superlative comparisons; do not judge whether the numbers are credible or valuable.
selected.rationale: R07, R13, and R42 prominently feature precise gains and dramatic runtime comparisons, a reporting style plausibly shaped by persuasive audience expectations rather than quality alone.

selected.name: Names a specific live difficulty and what the work changes
selected.instruction: 0-10. Reading only the abstract, judge how precisely it identifies a specific unresolved technical difficulty and states concretely what its own contribution changes about that difficulty. Judge the substance of the stated difficulty and the stated change, in the context the abstract itself sets up. Explicitly do NOT reward the topic being fashionable, popular, timely or recognisable, and do NOT reward the presence of currently-popular model names, system names, benchmark names, acronyms or technique labels; a plainly written abstract about an unfashionable, narrow or decades-old problem can score 10. 10 = the abstract names a particular failure mode, limitation or open question, says specifically why existing approaches do not resolve it, and states what its contribution establishes about it, precisely enough that a reader could say what would count as progress on it. 5 = a genuine difficulty is gestured at, but either the gap or the change is stated only in general terms. 0 = no unresolved difficulty is identified, or the only gap offered is that a popular method has not yet been pointed at a setting, with nothing said about what makes that hard.
selected.rationale: The conjectured upstream cause, working on what the field is currently active about, can genuinely produce engagement with a live open difficulty, and can separately produce a vocabulary fingerprint. This criterion keeps only the first by asking what difficulty is named and what changes, and by forbidding credit for fashionable vocabulary. Dissociation direction one: a five-sentence abstract on a classical estimator, containing no currently-popular term at all, which names an exact regime where the standard estimator is inconsistent, says why existing corrections fail there, and states the condition under which its own correction holds, scores near 10 here and near 0 on the surface component. Dissociation direction two: an abstract in which every sentence carries several fashionable model and method names but which says only that these are combined and evaluated, naming no difficulty and no change, scores near 10 on the surface component and near 0 here.
member_names: Names a specific live difficulty and what the work changes

selected.name: Density of currently-fashionable model, method and benchmark terms
selected.instruction: 0-10, extent only. Estimate how densely the abstract is packed with terms that are currently fashionable in the field: named popular models or systems, popular technique and paradigm labels, popular benchmark names, and buzz-phrases of the moment. Judge only how much of this vocabulary is present, roughly as the share of contentful words that are such terms, together with how often they recur. You are explicitly NOT deciding whether using such terms is good, bad, warranted, or a sign of anything, and you are NOT judging the research, the topic, the claims or the writing. 0 = no such terms anywhere. 3 = one or two such terms, used once each. 5 = a handful, roughly one or two per sentence in places. 8 = most sentences carry at least one, and several carry more than one. 10 = the abstract is overwhelmingly packed, reading largely as a dense list of fashionable names and phrases.
selected.rationale: This is the pure carrier: the vocabulary fingerprint that the same upstream cause deposits, with every trace of merit stripped out, posed as a countable extent question. Dissociation direction one: the classical-estimator abstract above, with no fashionable term at all, scores near 0 here while scoring near 10 on D01. Dissociation direction two: an abstract that lists every fashionable model and benchmark in the field and asserts only that they were combined, with no difficulty named and no change stated, scores 10 here and near 0 on D01. Because the question is answerable by counting words, no amount of substance can raise it and no absence of substance can lower it.
member_names: Density of currently-fashionable model, method and benchmark terms
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Trendy Topic Jargon Density

selected.name: Concrete checkable specifics conveyed, judged independently of length
selected.instruction: 0-10. Judge how many distinct, concrete, checkable specifics the abstract actually conveys about the work: what precisely was done, to or on what, under what stated conditions, compared against what alternative, and with what stated scope condition, assumption or limitation. Score the specifics themselves, not the amount of text carrying them: mentally normalise against the shortest text that could have carried them, and explicitly do NOT reward word count, sentence count, paragraph breaks, elaboration, subordinate clauses, restatement, or how thorough the work is made to sound. A three-sentence abstract can score 10, and a long multi-paragraph one can score 0. 10 = several independent specifics, each stated definitely enough that a reader could say what would have to be true for it to hold, including at least one stated condition or limit. 5 = the object of study and the approach are concrete, but conditions, comparisons and limits are left general. 0 = every statement is a generality that could describe dozens of different papers; nothing is pinned to a particular object, condition or comparison, however many words are spent.
selected.rationale: Length has a legitimate correlate: an author with more definite things to say may need more words, so elaboration and specificity are entangled. This criterion keeps the specificity and discards the words by forcing normalisation against the shortest text that could carry the same content and by naming length as ineligible for credit. Dissociation direction one: a terse three-sentence abstract that states the exact object, the exact comparison, and the regime in which the result fails scores near 10 here and near 0 on the surface component. Dissociation direction two: a four-paragraph abstract of long clauses that restates the motivation three times and never names a condition, comparison or limit scores 10 on the surface component and near 0 here.
member_names: Concrete checkable specifics conveyed, judged independently of length

selected.name: Sheer amount of text: words, sentences, clauses, paragraph breaks
selected.instruction: 0-10, extent only. Report how much text is present, using only word count, sentence count, average sentence length or number of subordinate clauses, and number of paragraph breaks. Do NOT consider what is claimed, how specific it is, whether the length is appropriate, well used, padded, or a sign of anything at all; you are not judging the writing or the research. 0 = extremely terse, roughly one to three short sentences. 3 = a short single paragraph, roughly four or five plain sentences. 5 = a typical single-paragraph abstract of moderate length with some multi-clause sentences. 8 = clearly longer than typical, or broken into more than one paragraph, with many multi-clause sentences. 10 = unusually long and multi-paragraph, with many long heavily subordinated sentences throughout.
selected.rationale: This is the fingerprint with no merit content whatsoever: it can be answered by counting tokens and line breaks without understanding a single claim. Dissociation direction one: the terse but fully specified three-sentence abstract scores near 0 here and near 10 on D03. Dissociation direction two: a long, multi-paragraph, heavily subordinated abstract that says nothing concrete scores 10 here and near 0 on D03. Nothing an author can do to raise substance raises this score, and nothing about emptiness lowers it.
member_names: Sheer amount of text: words, sentences, clauses, paragraph breaks
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Abstract length and sentence-count verbosity

selected.name: Protocol stated precisely enough for an independent re-run
selected.instruction: 0-10. Judge how precisely the abstract states the concrete commitments of the work, such that an independent reader could say what would have to be set up and run to put the claim to the test: the specific object or setting studied, the specific procedure or construction used, the specific comparison or control it is put against, the conditions or scale at which it is evaluated, and the stated boundary within which the claim is asserted to hold. Explicitly do NOT reward any mention or promise of released code, data, models, checkpoints, project pages, repositories, or URLs, and do not reward statements that the work is reproducible or open; an abstract containing no release sentence at all can score 10, and an abstract promising every artifact can score 0. Judge only how determinate the described work is. 10 = the setting, the procedure, the comparison and the evaluation conditions are each pinned down, and a boundary or assumption is stated; a reader could enumerate what would need re-running. 5 = the setting and procedure are determinate but the comparison or the conditions are left open. 0 = the described work could be instantiated in many mutually inconsistent ways; nothing about setting, procedure, comparison or conditions is pinned down.
selected.rationale: The conjectured upstream cause, an author's reproducibility practice, plausibly produces both a determinate, re-runnable description of the work and, separately, an advertisement that artifacts exist. This criterion keeps the first and bans credit for the second outright. Dissociation direction one: a short abstract with no release sentence and no URL, which names the exact setting, the exact procedure, the baseline it is measured against and the assumption under which the result holds, scores near 10 here and 0 on the surface component. Dissociation direction two: an abstract whose final sentence advertises code, data, pretrained checkpoints and a project page with a URL, but whose body says only that a novel framework achieves strong performance on standard settings, scores 10 on the surface component and near 0 here.
member_names: Protocol stated precisely enough for an independent re-run

selected.name: Extent of code, data, model and project-page release advertising
selected.instruction: 0-10, extent only. Report how much the abstract advertises artifacts: count how many distinct artifact types are mentioned or promised (for example code, data, models or checkpoints, project or demo pages), whether a concrete link or repository is given, how prominently the advertising is placed, and how often it recurs. You are explicitly NOT deciding whether releasing artifacts is good, whether the artifacts would be useful, complete, usable or reproducible, and you are not judging the research in any way. 0 = no mention of any artifact being available or promised. 3 = one artifact type mentioned in passing, no link. 5 = one or two artifact types clearly promised. 8 = several artifact types promised, or one promised together with a concrete link. 10 = multiple artifact types plus a concrete link or repository, advertised prominently and referred to more than once.
selected.rationale: This is the carrier alone, answerable by spotting release sentences and links without assessing anything about the work. Dissociation direction one: the short, link-free, fully determinate abstract described above scores 0 here while scoring near 10 on D05. Dissociation direction two: an otherwise vacuous abstract that promises code, data, checkpoints and a project page with a URL scores 10 here and near 0 on D05. Merit cannot raise this score and its absence cannot lower it.
member_names: Extent of code, data, model and project-page release advertising
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Artifact-release signaling
